localChanges: When a city can no longer build what it was building in the middle of your turn (an advance from a goody hut or a Diplomat, or a captured city), the city screen and lists now show it at once, rather than at the next turn (closes #978).

A city you capture while your government is below a Republic starts in civil disorder, as in Civilization: its next turn's shields are lost and you can't buy units in it until order is restored (closes #1014).
A land unit aboard a ship at sea stays asleep there, and a ship sailing on at sea puts any cargo you woke back to sleep. Cargo at sea is no longer offered Explore or Automate (closes #1031).
A new city's square is irrigated only where the land can be irrigated, so a city founded on Forest, Jungle or Swamp no longer gets free food once it's cleared (#1029).

log: `payRansom` asked for the victor's gold treasury and threw "Wrong number of playerTreasuries: 0" when there was none. It now pays nothing, and raises no `barbarians:ransom`, for a player with no gold treasury (civ-clone/web-renderer#963). In a game every player who can beat a leader has one, so play is unchanged.

lib/events gains emitBuildingCancelled(cityBuild, item, reason, engine), which emits city:building-cancelled with the build, the item it stopped building and why, for a ruleset's BuildingCancelled rule to call, as emitBuildingComplete and emitBuildingHeld are called. A client can then show the build as it is now, even when it is dropped in the middle of its player's turn (civ-clone/web-renderer#978).

A new BuildingCancelled rule, civ1-city:city/building-cancelled/emit, runs before Auto chooses again and emits city:building-cancelled with the build, the item and the reason, through base-city-lifecycle's emitBuildingCancelled. Every way a build is dropped goes through CityBuild#cancel, so a client can show the build as it is now, even in the middle of its player's turn. getRules takes the engine as a second argument. Needs core-city-build with the item and reason given to the rules, and base-city-lifecycle with emitBuildingCancelled (civ-clone/web-renderer#978).

A city founded on Arctic, Forest, Jungle, Mountains, Swamp or Tundra no longer gets Irrigation on its square, so clearing a city's Forest, Jungle or Swamp no longer leaves free irrigation behind. A city on Desert, Grassland, Hills, Plains or a River is still irrigated, with or without water nearby, as in v474.05 (civ-clone/web-renderer#1029).

civ1-government 0.1.6 puts a Democracy that civil disorder brings down into Anarchy even when the Anarchy lasts no turns (the Pyramids), with the new government due at once (civ-clone/web-renderer#1018). The collapse test now expects that, and a new test checks that the cities judged after the collapsing one that turn see Anarchy.

As v474.05 (`CAPTURE.C` `capunit`: `if (a == civnow && civ_gov[civnow] < 4) townbuf[b].status |= CITY_DISORDER;`), a city the human captures under Anarchy, Despotism, Monarchy or Communism is put in civil disorder at once. Its disorder is recorded on capture, after the old statuses are forgotten, so buying in it is refused and it's owed "order restored". The record carries a note of the turn the capture put it there, and a `CivilDisorder` rule holds to it until the city's next production has been lost, as `city_process` zeroes the shields while the flag is up (`CITYMGT.C`). Food is stored as usual. Then the city is judged by its citizens: it stays in disorder, or the record ends with `city:order-restored`. A city captured during the human's own turn start waits for its next turn. The note lives in the saved record. Computer captors, and a human under a Republic or Democracy, are unaffected (civ-clone/web-renderer#1014).
`capturedDisorder` is exported so a computer player (simple-ai-client, playing the human's Automate) can tell that such a city can't be calmed.

A land unit aboard a ship at sea is asleep (`Stowed`) from boarding, with no moves that turn, as in v474.05, and from the next turn it can be disbanded. It isn't offered Sleep, Explore or Automate there. Once it's picked out of the stack (woken), Sleep puts it back as it boarded: `Stowed`, with no moves left, not `Sleeping`, which would wake when a foreign unit comes into sight, and v474.05 never wakes a land unit at sea (`validate_record`). A ship that sails on at sea puts any awake land cargo back to sleep, as v474.05's move does (`status |= 1`). Into port, cargo is left as it was. Aircraft aboard a Carrier are unchanged (civ-clone/web-renderer#1031).
The at-sea Sleep is a `Sleep` subclass in `lib/sleepAboard.ts`, named `Sleep` because the renderer and its translations know an action by its class's name.

A new BuildingCancelled rule, civ2-city:city/building-cancelled/emit, registered before Auto's, emits city:building-cancelled with the build, the item and the reason, through base-city-lifecycle's emitBuildingCancelled, as civ1-city does. A client can then show the build as it is now, even in the middle of its player's turn. Needs core-city-build with the item and reason given to the rules, and base-city-lifecycle with emitBuildingCancelled (civ-clone/web-renderer#978).

CityBuild#cancel now processes the BuildingCancelled rules with the item it stopped building and the reason it was given (cancelled, unavailable, captured, or a ruleset's own), as well as the build. A city on Auto that can no longer build its item has already gone on to its queue by the time the rules run, so cleared() no longer says what was dropped or why. Rules that take only the build are unaffected (civ-clone/web-renderer#978).

civ1-city-happiness puts a city the human captures below a Republic in civil disorder until its next turn's production is lost, whatever its citizens think, and the Automate AI plays the human's turns as a client that counts as the human's. `DisorderPolicy` gains `beyondCalming`, for disorder a city's citizens and builds can't end this turn: such a city is neither calmed with Entertainers nor switched to a Temple and hurried, and isn't left among the uncalmed cities that raise the luxury rate. Civ1's policy says so of a city whose disorder is only its capture's (`capturedDisorder`), which `wasInDisorder`, and so the trade rates, no longer count either (civ-clone/web-renderer#1014).
This needs civ1-city-happiness with `capturedDisorder`, so it's released first.
